name.text: Selecting student committees and counting handshakes at a meeting

questiontext.text:
(a) A committee of \({@pr1@}\) students is to be chosen from a class of \({@pn1@}\). In how many ways can this be done?

Number of ways = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) There are \({@pn2@}\) people at a meeting and everyone shakes hands with everyone else exactly once. How many handshakes take place?

Number of handshakes = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Because order does not matter in either selection, use the combination formula:

\(\displaystyle {}_nC_r = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}\)

Part (a): Choosing a committee of {@pr1@} students from {@pn1@} students
A committee has no ranked roles, so selecting the same \({@pr1@}\) students in any order counts as one committee. Substitute \(n = {@pn1@}\) and \(r = {@pr1@}\), simplify \(({@pn1@} - {@pr1@})! = {@rem1@}!\), and cancel \({@rem1@}!\):

\(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@pr1@}} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,({@pn1@} - {@pr1@})!} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,{@rem1@}!} = \frac{{@num1_factors@} \times {@rem1@}!}{({@den1_factors@}) \times {@rem1@}!} = \frac{{@num1_factors@}}{{@den1_factors@}} = \frac{{@num1_prod@}}{{@den1_prod@}} = {@ta1@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of ways} = {@ta1@} }\)

Part (b): Counting handshakes among {@pn2@} people
Each handshake involves \(r = 2\) people, and person A shaking person B's hand is the same handshake as B shaking A's. Substitute \(n = {@pn2@}\) and \(r = 2\), simplify \(({@pn2@} - 2)! = {@rem2@}!\), and cancel \({@rem2@}!\):

\(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_{2} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{2!\,({@pn2@} - 2)!} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{2!\,{@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@num2_factors@} \times {@rem2@}!}{(2 \times 1) \times {@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@num2_factors@}}{2 \times 1} = \frac{{@num2_prod@}}{2} = {@ta2@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of handshakes} = {@ta2@} }\)

questiondescription.text:
Combinations in Real-Life Contexts: Committees and Handshakes

Grade 11 CBE: Evaluating unordered selections using nCr = n!/[r!(n - r)!] for committees and pairwise handshakes.

node.description: Check if student computed permutations nPr instead of combinations nCr

truefeedback.text: You calculated permutations \({}_{{@pn1@}}P_{{@pr1@}} = {@ta1_perm@}\), which treats different orderings of the same students as distinct committees. Because order does not matter, divide by \({@pr1@}! = {@den1_prod@}\): evaluate \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@pr1@}} = \frac{{@ta1_perm@}}{{@den1_prod@}}\).

node.description: Check if student computed n^r allowing repetition and order

truefeedback.text: You calculated \({@pn1@}^{{@pr1@}} = {@ta1_rep@}\), which allows the same student to be picked repeatedly and counts order. Choose \({@pr1@}\) distinct students without order using \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@pr1@}} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,{@rem1@}!}\).

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Order does not matter on a committee, so use combinations: \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@pr1@}} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,{@rem1@}!} = \frac{{@num1_prod@}}{{@den1_prod@}}\).

node.description: Check if student double-counted handshakes as n(n - 1)

truefeedback.text: You calculated \({@pn2@} \times {@pn2 - 1@} = {@ta2_perm@}\), which counts A shaking B's hand separately from B shaking A's hand. Divide by \(2! = 2\) to avoid counting each handshake twice: \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_2 = \frac{{@ta2_perm@}}{2}\).

You calculated \({@pn2@}^2 = {@ta2_sq@}\), which includes people shaking their own hands and counts each pair twice. Choose \(2\) distinct people without order: \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_2 = \frac{{@pn2@} \times {@pn2 - 1@}}{2}\).

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Each handshake chooses a pair of \(2\) people where order does not matter: evaluate \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_2 = \frac{{@pn2@} \times {@pn2 - 1@}}{2}\).
